text:
emma: Kicking off a config-only deploy for routing + batching + timeouts. No model/code changes. Deploy window 02:00-03:00 UTC tonight. Will start with a 5% canary, then 25% if metrics look good, then full. deploy-bot: Deploy initiated: cfg-v20240715-rc3 -> staging -> canary (5%). Link: https://deploy.redwood.internal/deploys/1719234567 :rocket:
raj: noted. Which exact params are changing?
kai: TL;DR:
- routing.policy: prefer-region-cost (fallback: region-latency)
- concurrency.per-queue: 80 -> 110
- request.timeout_ms: 20000 -> 12000
- batching: max_batch_tokens 4096 -> 3072, max_wait_ms 15 -> 8
- kv_cache.prefetch: enabled -> enabled (ttl unchanged)
- config-version: cfg-v20240715-rc3 (pin on canary)
maria: Thanks. Oncall thresholds? What should we rollback on?
emma: Rollback triggers: immediate rollback if any of the following within 10m of canary start:
- 5xx error rate > 0.5% (absolute) OR spike > 300% vs baseline
- p99 latency increases > 20% absolute (compare to last 24h baseline)
- token cost per-req increases > 12% sustained over 5m
- queue drops / throttled requests > 0.2%
(declared in the rollout playbook)
raj: Observability hooks: add these charts to the canary dashboard: p50/p95/p99 latency, 5xx rate, tokens-per-request, qdepth per-queue, batch size distribution. also enable live traces for sample ids prefixed with CANARY-171923
ops-bot: (automation) Canary dashboard snapshot created: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/canary/1719234567
kai: Small note on batching: reducing max_batch_tokens to 3072 to lower stall risk for short-chat workloads — we expect slightly higher per-token overhead but fewer tail latency outliers.
emma: Release notes snippet for public changelog (short):
```
- Performance: Adjusted inference routing and batching defaults to reduce tail latency for short-turn chat workloads. Reduced per-request timeout from 20s to 12s to recover capacity faster on stuck requests. (config-only)
- Ops: New rollout will be pinned to cfg-v20240715-rc3 during canary for safe rollback.
```
kai: internal release note (for eng):
- routing.policy: prefer-region-cost => should steer more traffic to cheaper regions with capacity headroom. watch cross-region ts latency.
- batching tuning: max_wait_ms reduced to 8ms to favor latency; expect mean batch size to drop ~10-15% for query traffic.
maria: Please add an alert for batch size < 1.5 on avg (means requests not batching) so we don't regress throughput unexpectedly.
emma: Good call, added to checklist.
raj: Quick sanity command if needed to abort: `curl -XPOST https://deploy.redwood.internal/api/v1/rollbacks -d '{"deploy_id":1719234567,"reason":"auto-rollback"}'`
deploy-bot: Canary at 5% complete. No immediate anomalies in first 3m. (reacted :eyes:)
kai: running smoke: grep traces for CANARY-171923 and sampling 20 traces. so far p99 aligns with baseline for prompt length < 256.
emma: If after 30m canary is green, we'll progress to 25% and keep a 15m observation window. If 25% is green, full rollout with staggered bump to 100% over 60m.
maria: I'm on standby for first 60m. Ping me in #oncall if anything crosses thresholds.
raj: note: infra autoscaler will pre-warm an extra node group during the 25% step to avoid transient throttles.
emma: Last ask: anyone object to proceeding?
kai: no objections from eng-releases. :+1:
raj: infra ok.
maria: oncall ok.
emma: OK starting now. tagging ops-bot to post a short release note in #announcements once full rollout completes.
ops-bot: Will post announcement on full completion.
deploy-bot: Progress update: moved to 25% at 1719235123, observe window active.
-- end of thread --
